ei.title: The Equal Odds Rule in Creative Brainstorming
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: AI is a prolific idea generator. Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately lean into variations of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on quantity. As Linus Pauling put it, "The best way to have a good idea is to have lots of ideas." Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative success is correlated to the total number of works created. Many studies have confirmed that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas (what Bob Sutton at a design and innovation consulting company called "idea ratio"), and one Stanford study pegged the number of ideas that distinguish a successful product from a failure at more than two thousand. This is why design thinking and innovation are so focused on the processes (what Utley and Klebahn call "idea flow") of creating possibilities without judgment.

questions.passage: AI is a (A)[prolific / scarce] idea generator. Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately lean into variations of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on (B)[quantity / scarcity]. As Linus Pauling put it, "The best way to have a good idea is to have lots of ideas." Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative success is correlated to the total number of works created. Many studies have confirmed that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas (what Bob Sutton at a design and innovation consulting company called "idea ratio"), and one Stanford study pegged the number of ideas that distinguish a successful product from a failure at more than two thousand. This is why design thinking and innovation are so focused on the processes (what Utley and Klebahn call "idea flow") of creating possibilities without (C)[judgment / approval].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① prolific — quantity — judgment: 원문 일치. AI는 다작의(prolific) 아이디어 생성기, 양(quantity)에 먼저 집중, 판단(judgment) 없이 가능성 창출 ←정답
❌ ② scarce — quantity — judgment: (A) scarce(부족한)는 prolific(다작의)의 반의어
❌ ③ prolific — scarcity — judgment: (B) scarcity(부족)는 quantity(양)와 반대 맥락
❌ ④ prolific — quantity — approval: (C) approval(승인)은 judgment(판단)과 의미 불일치

questions.passage: AI is a prolific idea generator. Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately lean into (A)[variations / repetitions] of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on quantity. As Linus Pauling put it, "The best way to have a good idea is to have lots of ideas." Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative success is (B)[correlated / unrelated] to the total number of works created. Many studies have confirmed that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas (what Bob Sutton at a design and innovation consulting company called "idea ratio"), and one Stanford study pegged the number of ideas that (C)[distinguish / blur] a successful product from a failure at more than two thousand. This is why design thinking and innovation are so focused on the processes (what Utley and Klebahn call "idea flow") of creating possibilities without judgment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① repetitions — correlated — distinguish: (A) repetitions(반복)은 variations(변형)와 의미 불일치
✅ ② variations — correlated — distinguish: 원문 일치. 첫 제안의 변형(variations)에 기대고, 창의적 성공은 총 작품 수와 상관관계(correlated)가 있으며, 성공 제품을 실패와 구별(distinguish) ←정답
❌ ③ variations — unrelated — distinguish: (B) unrelated(무관한)는 correlated(상관관계 있는)의 반의어
❌ ④ variations — correlated — blur: (C) blur(흐리게 하다)는 distinguish(구별하다)의 반의어
det.tip: lean into variations(변형에 기대다) / correlated to(~와 상관관계) / distinguish A from B(A를 B에서 구별)

Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative success is correlated to the total number of works created. Many studies have (A)[confirmed / denied] that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas (what Bob Sutton at a design and innovation (B)[consulting / manufacturing] company called "idea ratio"), and one Stanford study (C)[pegged / estimated] the number of ideas that distinguish a successful product from a failure at more than two thousand. This is why design thinking and innovation are so focused on the processes (what Utley and Klebahn call "idea flow") of creating possibilities without judgment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① confirmed — manufacturing — pegged: (B) manufacturing(제조)은 consulting(컨설팅)과 불일치
❌ ② denied — consulting — pegged: (A) denied(부인하다)는 confirmed(확인하다)의 반의어
✅ ③ confirmed — consulting — pegged: 원문 일치. 많은 연구가 확인했고(confirmed), 디자인·혁신 컨설팅(consulting) 회사, 수를 ~로 못 박았다(pegged) ←정답
❌ ④ confirmed — consulting — estimated: (C) estimated(추정하다)는 pegged(못 박다)와 유사하지만 원문은 pegged
det.tip: confirmed(확인하다) / consulting company(컨설팅 회사) / pegged the number at(~로 수를 못 박다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① quality — 원문 일치. 인간 그룹은 질(quality)에 집중한다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ② scarcity — 원문은 quantity(양). 좋은 아이디어는 양에 집중할 때 나온다는 맥락에서 scarcity(부족)는 부적절 ←정답
❌ ③ correlated — 원문 일치. 창의적 성공이 총 작품 수와 상관관계(correlated)가 있다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ judgment — 원문 일치. 판단(judgment) 없이 가능성을 만든다는 맥락에 적절

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① prolific — 원문 일치. AI가 다작의(prolific) 아이디어 생성기라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② confirmed — 원문 일치. 많은 연구가 확인했다(confirmed)는 맥락에 적절
✅ ③ equate — 원문은 distinguish(구별하다). 성공 제품을 실패와 구별하는 맥락에서 equate(동일시하다)는 부적절 ←정답
❌ ④ innovation — 원문 일치. 디자인 사고와 혁신(innovation)이라는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: distinguish A from B(A를 B에서 구별하다) ↔ equate(동일시하다)

questions.passage:
(A) Many studies have confirmed that creative quality <u>comes</u> from quantity of ideas.

(B) She <u>comes</u> from a small town in the countryside.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 comes에 대한 설명으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) comes from = 기인하다(~에서 나오다), (B) comes from = 출신이다(~에서 오다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A)와 (B) 모두 '도착하다' — 두 문장 모두 arrive의 의미가 아님
❌ ② (A)는 '도착하다', (B)는 '기인하다' — (A)는 기인하다, (B)는 출신이다
✅ ③ (A)는 '기인하다', (B)는 '출신이다' — (A) quality comes from quantity = 질이 양에서 기인한다, (B) She comes from a town = 그녀는 ~출신이다 ←정답

questions.passage: AI is a prolific idea generator. Human brainstorming groups tend to focus on the quality of creative ideas and almost immediately lean into variations of first suggestions, but good ideas are more likely when groups focus first on quantity. As Linus Pauling put it, "The best way to have a good idea is to have lots of ideas." Psychologist Dean Keith Simonton called this the "equal odds rule" arguing that creative success is correlated to the total number of works created. Many studies have confirmed that creative quality comes from quantity of ideas (what Bob Sutton at a design and innovation consulting company called "idea ratio"), and one Stanford study pegged the number of ideas that distinguish a successful product from a failure at more than two thousand. This is why design thinking and innovation are so focused on the processes (what Utley and Klebahn call "idea flow") of ____.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: selecting the best ideas through strict evaluation
eliminating weak ideas from the process
refining a single concept to perfection

det.analysis:
❌ ① selecting the best ideas through strict evaluation(엄격한 평가를 통해 최고 아이디어 선별) — 판단 없이가 핵심인 맥락과 반대
✅ ② creating possibilities without judgment(판단 없이 가능성 창출) — 원문 일치. 디자인 사고와 혁신이 판단 없이 가능성을 만드는 과정에 집중한다는 맥락 ←정답
❌ ③ eliminating weak ideas from the process(약한 아이디어 제거) — 양에 집중하고 판단을 보류한다는 맥락과 반대
❌ ④ refining a single concept to perfection(하나의 개념을 완벽하게 다듬기) — 많은 아이디어 생성이 핵심인 맥락과 반대
det.tip: without judgment = 판단 없이 = 아이디어 흐름(idea flow)의 핵심
